item.title: Heavy fermions emerge at an atomic-layer interface, unlocking new ways to design quantum materials
item.description: A research team led by the University of Osaka has directly observed, for the first time, an unusual heavy-fermion state forming at the boundary between a one-atom-thick material and a metal. Such states are closely linked to exotic quantum phenomena, including unconventional superconductivity, and the finding opens new possibilities for designing quantum materials through their interfaces.

item.description: By superimposing two ultrashort laser pulses that converge from different directions, a team of physicists at the University of Oldenburg has succeeded in generating three-dimensional light fields.

item.title: Time-stretch spectroscopy breaks temporal aliasing barrier
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02006-x A temporally super-resolved single-shot method overcomes the long-standing temporal–spectral trade-off in time-stretch spectroscopy. The outcome is continuous measurements of non-repetitive spectral dynamics with picosecond resolution, providing a three-orders-of-magnitude improvement over the current state of the art.

item.title: Optomechanics for piconewton force metrology
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02011-0 Of the sensors that can directly sense forces in the pico- and sub-pico-newton ranges, only a few can measure in liquids. Microfibre-based microcantilevers now add to this family, providing a versatile, broad-bandwidth, high-sensitivity optomechanical sensor.
